tagline: We make a number for every game. We bet the ones where the market's wrong.

games.matchup: Boston Celtics @ Detroit Pistons — NBA opening night
games.our_fair: Celtics 51.8% / Pistons 48.2% (devigged Pinnacle); spread cover fair BOS 49.5% / DET 50.5%; total Over-220 fair 51.0%
games.take: The two best teams in the East from last season open the year in the afternoon slot. Jayson Tatum returns after missing most of last season with an Achilles tear, and he has new company — Paul George arrived in the Jaylen Brown trade and Mitchell Robinson signed in the summer. Detroit kept the 60-win core together around Cade Cunningham and added John Collins. The market opened Pistons -2.5 and steamed all the way to Celtics -1.5, with the total falling four points to 220. Our number says it's priced about right: fair 51.8% against -113's 53.1% implied. No true edge — but the lean is the Pistons. Detroit's league-best defense gets the plus-money side at home against a Celtics team playing its first meaningful minutes together.
games.title: Celtics @ Pistons

games.matchup: Philadelphia 76ers @ New York Knicks — banner night at MSG
games.our_fair: Knicks 61.7% / Sixers 38.3% (devigged Pinnacle); spread cover fair NYK 50.2% / PHI 49.8%; total Over-232.5 fair 49.8%
games.take: Ring night. The defending-champion Knicks hang the banner and didn't list a single player on the injury report — continuity is the edge in openers. Philadelphia starts the LeBron James era (he and Jaylen Brown debut) alongside Embiid, Maxey and VJ Edgecombe, but it's a brand-new roster still finding its rhythm, and the center rotation behind Embiid is thin with Hukporti out for the season (Achilles) and Bona questionable. Our number has the Knicks at 61.7% against -169's 62.8% implied — priced right, no true edge. But the lean is New York: full health, banner-night energy, and a team that already knows exactly what it is.
games.title: 76ers @ Knicks
games.venue: Madison Square Garden, New York NY (indoor)

games.matchup: Oklahoma City Thunder @ San Antonio Spurs — WCF rematch
games.our_fair: Spurs 50.5% / Thunder 49.5% (devigged Pinnacle); spread cover fair OKC +1 50.5% / SAS -1 49.5%; total Over-231.5 fair 49.3%
games.take: The late game is the marquee: a rematch of last spring's seven-game Western Conference finals, which San Antonio won before falling to the Knicks in the Finals. The Athletic calls these clubs co-favorites for the 2027 title, and tonight is the first measurement of that claim. OKC gets Chet Holmgren back after a quad contusion wiped out his preseason; San Antonio opens without Tobias Harris (calf) but with Wembanyama, Fox, Castle and Harper intact. Our number is a pure coin flip — 50.5/49.5 — so there's no true edge. The lean is the Spurs at home, by a hair: Finals-run continuity and the best player on the floor.
games.title: Thunder @ Spurs
games.venue: Frost Bank Center, San Antonio TX (indoor)

games.matchup: Missouri State Bears (2-4) @ Delaware Blue Hens (2-4) — Conference USA
games.our_fair: Delaware 56.3% / Missouri State 43.7% (devigged Pinnacle); spread cover fair DEL 51.5% / MOST 48.5%; total Over-53 fair 49.3%
games.take: Both teams are 2-4 and both have quarterback questions. Delaware's Nick Minicucci is week-to-week, but Tyler Bell threw for 306 yards and 2 TD in his first career start (a 33-30 loss to MTSU). Missouri State got its first CUSA win last week on a walk-off field goal, with Henry Belin IV breaking through and Isaiah Myers leading the conference in receiving. The market leaned Delaware's way since the open. Fair is 56.3% against -135's 57.4% implied — no edge. But the lean is Missouri State: the number has fully priced Bell's debut, and the Bears' passing game (Myers, 73% completions last week) attacks the worst part of Delaware's defense.
games.title: Missouri State @ Delaware

games.matchup: Middle Tennessee Blue Raiders @ FIU Panthers — Conference USA
games.our_fair: FIU 78.6% / MTSU 21.4% (devigged Pinnacle); spread cover fair 50.0% / 50.0%; total Over-46 fair 48.1%
games.take: FIU is undefeated at Pitbull Stadium this season, and the market has priced that home dominance at nearly 80% win probability. The caveat: FIU QB JJ Kohl sits at a 7/7 TD-to-INT ratio and the Panthers run for just 3.4 yards per carry — you can't turn the ball over and expect to win by margin. MTSU is 1-1 in CUSA after last week's 33-30 win at Delaware. Fair 78.6% against -393's 79.7% implied — no true edge. The lean is FIU: home-field form, the better defense, and a MTSU offense that needed extra help to beat a 2-4 team last week.
games.title: Middle Tennessee @ FIU

games.matchup: South Alabama Jaguars (4-2) @ Marshall Thundering Herd (3-3) — Sun Belt
games.our_fair: South Alabama 59.0% / Marshall 41.0% (devigged Pinnacle); spread cover fair USA 49.8% / MARSH 50.2%; total Over-65 fair 50.0%
games.take: The Sun Belt shootout of the night: South Alabama ranks 7th nationally in scoring (52 vs ULM, 56 vs Arkansas State), runs the ball at the 8th-highest rate in the country, and is 2-0 in league play. Marshall is 3-3, 0-2 in conference, 1-5 against the spread, and its defense ranks 120th in yards allowed. The 65 total signals an expectation of plenty of offense. Fair 59.0% against -151's 60.2% implied — no true edge at this price. The lean is the Jaguars: the best offense on the field against a defense that has shown it can't stop anyone.
